statement: Fix E in the interior of J and s ∈ R. The following statements hold. 1. At ζ = E + (s + iy)/n, in the order n → ∞ and then y → ∞, the diagonal Gvv(ζ) at a uniform vertex, jointly with every fixed ordered neighborhood of potentials around v, converges to the tree diagonal mo(E + i0) with the corresponding tree environment. For any fixed number of independently sampled vertices the joint assertion holds with independent tree environments, and their off-diagonal Green entries tend to zero in probability. The diagonal assertion also holds along every sequence nη → ∞, (e, η) → (E, 0). 2. There are c, C > 0 such that, for every sufficiently large fixed y, lim sup n→∞ P  ℑ 1 n Tr G  E + s + iy n  − πρd,w(E) > y−c  ≤ Cy−c . (31) The constants are independent of the fixed real number s. 3. For each fixed s ∈ R and y > 0, the sampled diagonal imaginary parts are uniformly integrable in the following limiting sense: lim T→∞ lim sup n→∞ EH,v  ℑGvv  E + s + iy n  1{ℑGvv(E+(s+iy)/n)>T}  = 0. (32) The double-limit assertion in the first item means that, for bounded continuous tests, the limsup of the discrepancy as n → ∞ tends to zero as y → ∞.
